label: Scenario 1
title: Scenario 1: the harness reads the label and picks the zone and arm, WALLX picks the bag up and puts it into that zone

steps.title: Harness call (read the label, choose zone + arm, build the WALLX prompt)
steps.detail: Barcode reader first, pincode OCR reader as fallback. Pincode 940/941/950/951 → zone 1 → left arm; 900-902 → zone 2 → right arm; else zone 3. The zone number and arm are written into the WALLX sentence.
steps.prompt: Read the label with the barcode reader (pincode OCR reader as fallback), choose the zone and the arm.

steps.title: WALLX picks the bag up and puts it into the zone
steps.detail: WALLX (wall-x 2610-dualhead-v2, organisers' server) starts from rest. Every call it gets the HEAD camera image (black wrist images) + both arms' state + the sentence above and returns an action chunk for both arms. The harness LOCKS the arm the zone does not use, runs 40% of each chunk per call (--slow 0.4) and keeps the same sub-goal (--no-reset-on-subgoal). 60 calls. WALLX alone does the grasp, the lift, the carry and the set-down.

steps.title: Harness call (release)
steps.detail: The acting claw opens fully where WALLX left it, then lifts 8 cm straight up.
steps.prompt: Open the claw fully and lift straight up.

steps.title: Harness call (both arms home)
steps.detail: Harness call of both arms to home (≤ 5 cm per call).
steps.prompt: Both arms: go to rest.

steps.title: Done
steps.detail: Session ends; video, every call (state, actions, images) and the log are saved.

label: Scenario 4
title: Scenario 4: right arm picks the Bhindi box, hands it to the left arm in the air, WALLX puts it into zone 1

steps.title: Harness call (read the label, route to zone 1)
steps.detail: Barcode reader first, pincode OCR reader as fallback. Code 420/95126/001 = pincode 951 → zone 1 → left arm.
steps.what: label → lane → acting arm → target zone
steps.prompt: Read the label with the barcode reader (pincode OCR reader as fallback), choose the zone and the arm.

steps.title: Harness call (pick + handover)
steps.detail: Harness call (32 rows per call): the right arm picks the box and hands it to the left claw in the air.

sub.text: right arm moves from home to above the box (claw closed)
right claw opens and lowers around the box
right claw closes on the box (grasp)
right arm lifts the box to the handover point (~18 cm up, table centre)
left claw opens and reaches in
left claw closes on the box: both claws hold it
right claw opens: the box is in the left claw only

steps.prompt: Right arm: pick up the purple box and hand it to the left arm in the air.

steps.title: Harness call (right arm backs off)
steps.detail: Harness call (≤ 4 cm per call): right claw lifts and moves away to (0.35, 0.20, 0.26) m so it cannot hit the box or the left arm.
steps.prompt: Right arm: let go and move up and away from the box.

steps.title: Harness call (right arm home)
steps.detail: Harness call to home, claw closed. From here the right arm stays parked.
steps.prompt: Right arm: go to rest.

steps.title: WALLX places the box into zone 1 (left arm)
steps.prompt: Stretch to the top left corner of the table and put the purple box into zone 1.
steps.detail: WALLX (wall-x 2610-dualhead-v2, organisers' server) gets the HEAD camera image (the harness sends black wrist images: the held box blocks the left wrist camera, so it only confuses WALLX) + both arms' state + this sentence every call, and returns an action chunk for both arms. The harness LOCKS the right arm (its WALLX actions are replaced by 'hold still'), runs 40% of each chunk per call (--slow 0.4, smoother and safer), and keeps the same sub-goal across calls (--no-reset-on-subgoal). 40 calls. WALLX alone decides where to move, how to lower and where to set the box down.

steps.title: Harness call (release)
steps.detail: The left claw opens fully where WALLX left it, then lifts 8 cm straight up, so the box stays inside zone 1.
steps.prompt: Open the claw fully and lift straight up.

steps.title: Harness call (both arms home)
steps.detail: Harness call of both arms to home (≤ 5 cm per call).
steps.prompt: Both arms: go to rest.

steps.title: Done
steps.detail: Session ends; video, every call (state, actions, images) and the log are saved.

label: Scenario 5
title: Scenario 5: WALLX goes for the cap; a person moves it; the harness, always watching, cancels the prompt and gives WALLX the new location

steps.title: Harness call (read the label, choose zone + arm)
steps.prompt: Read the label with the barcode reader (pincode OCR reader as fallback), choose the zone and the arm.
steps.detail: Cap label 90291 → zone 2 → right arm.

steps.title: Harness call (locate the cap on the 3x3 table grid)
steps.prompt: Find the cap on the head camera and name its grid cell.
steps.detail: Tracks the cap on the head camera and maps it to the table grid (back / middle / front x left / middle / right); the cell goes into the WALLX sentence.

steps.title: WALLX picks up the cap and puts it into zone 2 (the harness re-targets it when the cap is moved)
steps.detail: WALLX does all the motion (head camera + both gripper cameras, left arm locked, 110 calls). The harness keeps watching the cap on its grid every call: when the cap sits in a NEW cell for 3 calls, the current prompt is cancelled, WALLX's history is reset and it gets a new sentence with the new location (same target zone 2). Red marks on the timeline = re-targets.

steps.title: Harness call (release)
steps.prompt: Open the claw fully and lift straight up.
steps.detail: The right claw opens fully where WALLX left it, then lifts 8 cm.

steps.title: Harness call (right arm home)
steps.prompt: Right arm: go to rest.
steps.detail: The right arm goes to rest; the left arm never moved.

steps.title: Done
steps.detail: Session ends; video, every call (state, actions, images) and the log are saved.
